scope.method: Third disjoint batch of fifty currently held rows selected from remaining figurative/collocation candidates. Exact source, meaning, current hold reason and plausible owner scope were assessed. The three leads are conditional, not promotions.

usageEvidence.finding: Documents bread and butter as mainstay/livelihood and bread-and-butter as basic matters; this supports the idiom but does not resolve the grocery sentence literal/figurative ambiguity.

screenedRows.expression: one step ahead of the clock
screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: Preparing tonight keeps us one step ahead of the clock tomorrow.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Better prepared than the time pressure demands; a vivid extension of being ahead.
screenedRows.sourceQuestion: Can you suggest some ways to make sure you are not late for anything?
screenedRows.currentHoldReason: One step ahead of the clock may be an ad hoc blend; check idiomaticity and source context before making a target.
screenedRows.independentAssessment: The guide's “ahead of the clock” is an ad hoc clock blend. Owner 2171 anticipates delays, but its fixed “stay one step ahead of delays” construction and concrete travel-risk decision do not transfer to this clock sentence.

comparedOwner.titleEn: stay one step ahead of delays
comparedOwner.meaningEn: Anticipate likely delays and adjust plans before they disrupt you.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: A written plan helped hold the day together.

screenedRows.independentAssessment: The written plan keeps a day organised; “hold the day together” is a creative extension of hold together, with no bounded idiom or distinct decision established.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: Without a timer, the afternoon can run away with you.
screenedRows.sourceMeaning: Become difficult to control, especially time or emotion; a conventional figurative phrase.
screenedRows.sourceQuestion: Do you think it is easy to manage your time in the modern world?
screenedRows.currentHoldReason: The afternoon can run away with you sounds potentially awkward; confirm a natural time-escapes-you pattern before making it a lesson. Provisional editorial decision; independent review remains open.
screenedRows.independentAssessment: The intended loss of time control is understandable, but “the afternoon can run away with you” is not a secure natural unit. A normal “time got away from us” model would not match the source wording.

screenedRows.exactSourceSentence: Without a break, people can feel swallowed whole by routine.

screenedRows.currentHoldReason: Swallowed whole by routine is a striking passive metaphor, but may be less idiomatic than swallowed up by routine; verify naturalness. Provisional editorial decision; independent review remains open.
screenedRows.independentAssessment: Owner 1144 teaches a person feeling swallowed up by work. Routine as a consuming force is related, but “swallowed whole by routine” changes the target form and source intensity; source naturalness and a broader owner assessment must be proved first.

comparedOwner.meaningEn: Feel that work occupies so much time and attention that other parts of life are crowded out.

screenedRows.independentAssessment: The audience feels a sudden thrill from the clue. “A jolt of electricity” may evoke literal current, whereas owner 1232 teaches a shock that jolts people mentally awake; the expressions do not share a teachable construction.

comparedOwner.meaningEn: Abruptly make someone mentally alert or aware through a striking experience.
